FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 11 November 1975, after the draft finalized by the Timber Stores Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council.

0.2 This standard covers tile requirements of a wooden box intended for
housing microscope slides to ensure their proper handling and keeping. A proper index on the inner side of the lid will also provide information regarding details of the corresponding slide. 0.3 In the formulation of this standard due weightage has been given to international co-ordination among the standards and practices prevailing in different countries in addition to relating it to the practices in the field in this country.
G.t For-the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS: 2�1960* . The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard covers the requirements of a wooden box intended for keeping 100 microscope slides.
2. TERMINOLOGY

2.1 For the purpose of thiR standard, the defirIitions Riven in IS : 707-1968t shall apply.
*Rules for rounding off numeriea! values ( "vi"i ). tolOisaTy or tt'rms applicable to timber and tlmber products

(fi,,'

r'lIuw. ).

2

IS: 7858 - 1975

3. MATERIAL
3.1 Timber - The frame and slide rack of the box shall he manufactured from any of the species of timber given in Appendix A. Only one species of timber shall be used for the manufacture of anv one frame or slide rack in the box. 3.1.1 The timhcr shall be- well seasoned to a moisture content not exceeding 12 percent and the inclination of grain shall not exceed 1 in 10. The timber shall be free from centre heart (pith), sapwood (exc~pt in case of coniferous timbers and Haldu I, any kind of decay ( rot), shakes, insect attack, knots, cracks, splits and warp. 3.2 Plywoocl- The botton' and top of the box shall be manufactured from 5 mm thick plywood conforming to Type BC. WWR Grade of 18 : 303-1975*.

4. DIMENSIONS AND TOLERANCES
f.l The box shall conform to the dimensions as shown in Fig. I. 4.2 A tolerance of � 1 mm may be permitted on the overall dimensions of the box,

5. MANUPACTURE
5.1 The box shall be rectangular having two slide racks fitted in the body and a hinged lid at the top. The two racks shall have 50 grooves equally spaced, 2�7 mm wide, each numbered I to 100 to accommodate 50 slides in each row. The bottom and top of the box ( se, 3.2) shall be fixed to the frame with brass pins. Two brass hooks on the front of the hody shall he provided to enter the two corresponding eyes on the lid to ensure firm closure of the box. A paper index, which shall also he numbered I to 100 to carry necessary details of the corresponding slides, shall be pasted on the inside of the lid.

6.

WORKMAN~H1P

AND FINISH

6.1 The box shall be smoothly finished. The paper index shall also be neatly pasted to the inside of the lid. The box shall be varnished on the outside with a waterproof clear varnish to impart a good finish.

7. SAMPUNG
7.1 The method of drawing representative samples of boxes and the criteria for conformity shall be as prescribed in Appendix B.

8. MARKING
8.1 Unless otherwise specified, each box shall he J~Ribly and indelibly marked with the following information: a) Manufacturer's name or initials or recognized trade-mark, if any: h) Year of manufacture; and c) Species of timber ( see 3.1 and Appendix A ).

8.1.1 The wooden box may also he marked with Standard mark.
8.1.2 The use of the Standard Mark is govered by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from tbe Bureau of Indian Standards.

9. PACKING
9.1 Packing shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.

APPENDIX B
( ClauJe 7.1 )
SAMPLING OF WOODEN BOXES FOR MICROSCOPE SLIDES B-1. SAMPLING AND TESTING
B-l.1 Lot - In any consignment, &\11 the boxes manufactured under similar conditions of production shall be grouped together to constitute a Jot.

8-1.2 Vlsaal Examiaatioa -- All the boxes in the lot shall be inspected for visual defects, workmanship and finish, Any box failing to satisfy the requirements for these characteristics shall be rejected. Those boxes which
pass the visual examination shall lJe subjected to further tests.

8-1.3 SelectioD or Sample. for Further Tetrt. - The number of boxes
to be selected for further testing from those accepted as in B-l.2 shall be in accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 1.
